title: Kid Ross, Frank Torres's and playing at Josie Arlington's
summary: Kid Ross, a black-key pianist, befriends him and sends him up to play at Josie Arlington's, where he is shocked by the naked dancing.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Well, that's why I'm going to bring in Kid Ross. Yeah, okay. After I walked back in the district, and this fellow, George Spafford, was an electrician, took, you know, the cribs and all that, he sent me around Frank Torres. And Kid Ross was playing there, see? I mean, Kid Ross was in the room, uh, hearts was a great game in there. You know hearts?

And so that night, well, Kid Ross took me over the hotel and I got a good clean-up, see? I must have been dirty behind the ears from those trains and stuff. And Kid Ross was turned out to be a good friend of mine, see? And he was a black key artist. He played a nice piano. Black key artist. And one night they're playing, they're playing hearts. She didn't come down, let's say, go, Professor, Professor, the nigga made, Professor. And Kid Ross was playing Josie Allentons. And Kid says, go on up there. I said, oh, go on up there. I go up there, I'm like this trembling. You know, going to the swank room, all looking glasses, you know. They got a nigga gal there. I forgot what she was singing, but I played for it anyway. And all at once she says, come on, da-da-da-da-da-da-da-da. And I looked up and you could see a nigga gal swinging back there. Mm-hmm. I came down and I bawled the hell out about that. That was too much for me. Well, I was younger though. Hell, I could lay it up with women if I wanted. I wouldn't have enough to do with them. I thought too much of my mother. I said, well, if my mother see me laying here,
Well, they would get naked, those women? Well, they're naked and dance. See, there's this one. See, the rest are all. They used to sell forts for a dollar. If there's four or five men, five men.
